headline: Neptune’s strange moon setup explained
standfirst: Scientists are solving the mystery of why Neptune has one massive moon and many tiny ones.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Neptune has a weird imbalance. Its largest moon, Triton, holds 99% of the planet's satellite mass.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Triton orbits backward compared to Neptune's rotation. This suggests it was captured by the planet.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This capture likely caused chaos, destroying other moons and shaping the current ring system.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Researchers are using this data to map out how Neptune's moon system evolved over time.

caption:
Scientists are studying how Neptune captured its massive moon Triton and destroyed its original moon system.

Triton is a total outlier in the solar system. Its backward orbit and massive size compared to the tiny moons around it hint at a violent history where Neptune snagged it from space. This capture likely wiped out previous satellites.
